passage:
Tanvir, you said your friend Rohit has stopped coming to class? Let your Sudha Masi tell you about my friend Leena, back in college in Nagpur. She was the loudest girl in our hostel, always organising picnics. Then she failed economics in second year. Suddenly she was skipping lectures, sleeping till noon, changing the subject whenever anyone said "exam". The others lectured her: "You'll ruin your future!" She hid even more.
I didn't lecture. One morning I knocked with two cups of chai and said, "Come with me to the library for one hour. We'll just find out the re-exam date. That's all." She came. The next week we did one chapter together. She passed in December. So, beta, don't give your friend a speech. Give him company and one small step.

qa.q: Which subject did Leena fail?
qa.a: Economics, in second year.

qa.q: Why might Leena have hidden even more when the others lectured her?
qa.a: She probably felt ashamed about failing, and lectures made the shame bigger, so avoiding people and exams felt safer.

qa.q: What choice of Sudha's helped Leena, and why?
qa.a: Bringing chai and asking for just one hour to find the re-exam date, which offered company and a small step instead of pressure.

qa.q: How might Tanvir use this story with Rohit?
qa.a: Tanvir could skip the speech and offer Rohit company and one small, concrete step, like checking a date together.

grounding: An aunt tells how, as a student, she noticed a lively friend retreat after failing a subject and offered company and one small step instead of a lecture.

passage:
Two weeks before the supplementary exams, with the monsoon flooding the lanes around their hostel, Sarita noticed that Himani had stopped coming to anything. Himani, who usually sang in the corridor and dragged everyone to the chai stall, now slept through lectures and turned her face to the wall whenever anyone mentioned statistics, the paper she had failed.
Sarita had exams too, and hardly any money left for the month. She couldn't fix everything. On Tuesday she knocked with two packets of biscuits. "I'm not here to lecture," she said. "Let's just download last year's paper. Ten minutes. Then biscuits." Himani hesitated, then sat up. The Wi-Fi kept dropping in the rain, so they used Sarita's phone data. They opened the paper, read question one, and ate the biscuits.
On Wednesday, Himani knocked on Sarita's door.

qa.q: Which paper had Himani failed?
qa.a: Statistics.

qa.q: Why might Himani turn her face to the wall when statistics came up?
qa.a: Failing the paper probably left her ashamed and afraid, so avoiding the subject felt safer than facing it.

qa.q: What choice of Sarita's worked despite her own exams and little money, and why?
qa.a: Offering company and one small step, ten minutes to download last year's paper, instead of a lecture, which made starting feel possible. 🤍

qa.q: How might Sarita have felt when Himani knocked on her door on Wednesday?
qa.a: Probably relieved and quietly pleased, seeing that the small ten-minute visit had helped Himani take the next step herself.

grounding: In a flooded monsoon week a student notices her lively friend retreating after a failed paper and offers biscuits, company and one small step.

passage:
Rukmini was always the first to arrive at the college canteen in Andheri and the last to leave, arguing about films. So Kamal noticed when she disappeared. She had missed four accounts lectures in a row. When he texted, she sent jokes but ignored questions. When a classmate mentioned the ATKT form for the failed accounts paper, she suddenly remembered she had to "rush home".
Kamal didn't want to lecture her; everyone else already had. On Saturday he messaged: "Chai at the station stall at 5? I'll bring the ATKT form. We'll just fill in your name. Nothing else."
She came, late and quiet. They filled in her name and roll number. Then they talked about a film for an hour. On Monday she was back in the accounts lecture, sitting next to him.

qa.q: How many accounts lectures had Rukmini missed in a row?
qa.a: Four.

qa.q: Why did Rukmini suddenly have to 'rush home' when the ATKT form came up?
qa.a: The failed paper probably made her feel ashamed and anxious, so escaping the conversation gave quick relief.

qa.q: What choice did Kamal make, and why did it work?
qa.a: He skipped the lecture and offered chai with one tiny first step, just filling in her name on the form, which made facing it bearable.

qa.q: How might Kamal have felt seeing Rukmini back in the accounts lecture on Monday?
qa.a: Probably relieved and glad, since his small, no-lecture offer had helped her take the first step back.

grounding: A student notices a lively friend dodging classes and talk of a failed paper, and offers chai and one small concrete step instead of lectures.

passage:
Dilnaz caught up with Maria outside the chemistry block, where Maria was hurrying the other way.

"Maria! You weren't in lab again."

"Oh. Yeah. Overslept."

"Three Mondays in a row?"

Maria shrugged, laughing. "I'm a very committed sleeper."

"You also left chai yesterday the second Riz said 'organic'."

The laugh stopped. "Can we not? I know I failed it. Everyone's already told me what I should do."

"I'm not going to tell you anything." Dilnaz shifted her bag. "I'm going to Dr Pinto's office hour at three anyway. For my own doubt. Walk with me? You don't have to go in. Just see where the door is."

"...That's it?"

"That's it. Door. Then samosas."

Maria looked at the ground. "Three?"

"Three. I'll wait by the stairs."

At five to three, Maria was at the stairs, her hood up, but there.

qa.q: Where was Maria at five to three?
qa.a: Maria was at the stairs, her hood up, but there.

qa.q: Why might Maria joke about being "a very committed sleeper"?
qa.a: The joke keeps Dilnaz away from the painful subject of the failed paper. Maria seems ashamed and tired of being told what to do, so humour feels safer than the truth.

qa.q: Which choice of Dilnaz's made Maria willing to come, and why?
qa.a: Dilnaz promised not to lecture and offered one tiny step, just walking to the office door, with company and samosas after. It was small enough that Maria could say yes.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz have felt when Maria snapped, "Can we not?"
qa.a: Dilnaz was probably concerned but careful not to push; instead of lecturing, she offered to walk Maria to the office hour and wait by the stairs.

grounding: A friend notices a usually lively student dodging classes and talk of a failed subject, and offers company and one small first step instead of a lecture.

passage:
I'm Gopika, and this was in our second year of engineering in Thrissur. Arnab was the loudest person in quiz club. He ran it, basically. Then he failed Engineering Drawing, and he vanished.

At first I didn't connect it. He just missed quiz one week. Then he stopped coming to the drawing studio. In the canteen, if anyone said "backlog", he suddenly needed to take a call.

I wanted to shake him and say, "You'll lose a year!" But I remembered how I felt when my uncle lectured me after my twelfth results. I just curled up.

So one Friday I texted him: "I'm redoing my sheet 3 in the studio tomorrow at ten. Bring your pencils. We'll do one sheet. Just one."

He replied an hour later: "ok."

He came late. He did half the sheet. But he came back the Saturday after.

qa.q: What did Arnab suddenly need to do when someone in the canteen said "backlog"?
qa.a: He suddenly needed to take a call.

qa.q: Why did Gopika decide not to shake Arnab and warn him about losing a year?
qa.a: Gopika remembered feeling small and curling up when an uncle lectured after the twelfth results, and was worried a lecture would push Arnab further away.

qa.q: What was the turning point in how Gopika helped Arnab?
qa.a: Choosing a concrete invitation, one sheet in the studio at ten, instead of a warning. A specific small step with company was easier for Arnab to accept.

qa.q: What might the text "ok", an hour later, tell us about Arnab?
qa.a: It may show he was hesitant or embarrassed but still willing. The delay suggests saying yes wasn't easy for him.

grounding: A student notices a lively friend retreating after failing a subject and offers company and one concrete step rather than a lecture.
